 PAK vs ENG vs SL ODI Tri-series 2026: Who qualifies for final if two teams have same points and net run-rate?
 Soham Mukherjee
 •

 KEY TAKEAWAYS:
 Pakistan lead on four points, while England have lost both their games so far.
 The top two advance to the final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium on October 31.
 Tie-breaker rules explained if two teams are tied on points and NRR. 
 MORE:  Pakistan vs Sri Lanka vs England ODI Tri-series 2026: Who will qualify for final? Qualification scenarios explained 
 Explaining the tiebreakers: How finalists are determined if teams tie on points and NRR 
 A tight finish could leave two teams, or even all three, locked together at the end of the league stage of the ODI tri-series involving Pakistan, England and Sri Lanka, and the tiebreaker rules would then decide who plays the final.
 With each side still to play two matches, it is worth knowing how the final spots would be settled if points and net run rate cannot separate them.
 MORE:   Salman Agha breaks Mohammad Yousuf's record in Rawalpindi 
 Pakistan lead the table after wins over Sri Lanka and England, while Sri Lanka’s two-wicket victory over England, when they chased down 430, has kept them in contention. England have lost both of their matches and sit at the bottom.
 The table below is current as of October 23, 2026, and a win earns two points, while a no-result gives one point to each side.

 Pos Team Played Won Lost Points NRR 
 1 Pakistan 2 2 0 4 +1.240 
 2 Sri Lanka 2 1 1 2 -0.348 
 3 England 2 0 2 0 -0.892 
 Tri-series format and remaining fixtures at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore
 Each team plays four league games and the top two sides move on to the final on October 31. All of the remaining matches will take place at the Gaddafi Stadium in Lahore.
 Date Match Venue 
 Sunday, October 25 Pakistan vs England Lahore 
 Tuesday, October 27 Pakistan vs Sri Lanka Lahore 
 Thursday, October 29 Sri Lanka vs England Lahore 
 Saturday, October 31 Tri-series final Lahore 
 What is the tiebreaker rule if two teams finish level on points and net run rate?
 When teams end the league stage level on points, the tournament regulations apply a series of steps in order.
 The first is the number of wins, and the side with more victories across the league phase goes ahead. If that does not settle it, the team with the better net run rate over all four completed games is placed higher.
 Should two teams still be tied on points and on net run rate down to three decimal places, the head-to-head record comes next. The sides play each other twice in this tri-series, so a 2-0 advantage would end the contest straight away. If the two meetings are split 1-1, the tie is then broken by the net run rate in the matches between the two tied teams only.
 Beyond that, the usual ICC white-ball clauses favour the side that has taken more wickets per ball bowled, or has the lower bowling average, across the group phase. If every statistic remains level, the playing conditions allow for a drawing of lots or a formal seeding priority to decide the matter.
 Step Tiebreaker 
 1 Total number of wins in the league phase 
 2 Net run rate across all four completed league games 
 3 Head-to-head record (a 2-0 result settles the tie) 
 4 Net run rate in matches between the tied teams (if head-to-head is 1-1) 
 5 Bowling record: wickets per ball bowled or bowling average across the group phase 
 6 Drawing of lots or formal seeding priority 
 The three-way tie scenario: How a 2-2-2 finish could decide the final spots
 The most realistic route to a tie involves all three teams. If England win their remaining games, beating Pakistan and Sri Lanka, and Sri Lanka also beat Pakistan, each side would finish on two wins and two losses, with four points apiece.
 Wins would then be level, so the decision would come down to net run rate, which is worked out to three decimal places.
 MORE:   DK slammed for praising Brook after 'negative' reaction to Gill's 200 
 A detail that matters here is the treatment of teams who are bowled out. Under ICC playing conditions, if a side is dismissed before it has used its full 50 overs, its batting run rate is calculated as though it had faced all 50, and that can hurt a team badly after a collapse.
 England’s batting innings against Pakistan, when they were bowled out in 38.4 overs, shows how heavily such a result can weigh on the figures.
 Pakistan’s net run rate of +1.240 gives them a healthy cushion at present, while Sri Lanka and England will need big wins to make up ground in the closing matches.
